Paper: Flores & Olivares, MPHBS: A novel hybrid metaheuristic with SARSA-guided information exchange, Knowledge-Based Systems 352:117070
RL/learning mechanism: SARSA-style tabular update (dimension-wise contextual-bandit-like), Q indexed by (dimension, ranked row, source)
Information exchange level: Dimension-wise component assembly from ranked HBA/MPA memories
Group-wise exchange: No (explicitly dimension-wise; paper lists strong coupling as a threat to validity)
Main difference from LA-KAIE: Same HBA-MPA backbone and benchmarks. LA-KAIE replaces the per-dimension Q-table with a landscape-conditioned controller over exchange MODES (when/which source/granularity) and transfers estimated interaction groups.

Paper: Real Variable Interaction Crossover (RVIntX) - Variable Importance and Interaction in Differential Evolution: Online Learning and a New Recombination Operator (Springer LNCS chapter)
RL/learning mechanism: Online linkage learning (variable importance and interaction) inside DE
Landscape awareness: No landscape-state controller reported in abstract
Main difference from LA-KAIE: CLOSE OVERLAP on the group-preserving recombination idea. Differences (per abstract only): single-population DE crossover, no controller that decides when to exchange or dimension-vs-group granularity, no cross-population source selection.
Evidence available: Search snippet / abstract only (full text blocked)

Paper: Using Variable Interaction Graphs to Improve Particle Swarm Optimization (VIGPSO), GECCO 2025 (extended arXiv 2509.06985)
RL/learning mechanism: Online learning of a variable interaction graph from Pearson correlations of particle updates
Variable interaction modeling: YES - learned VIG from population dynamics (no extra FEs)
Group-wise exchange: Partially - VIG modifies continuous trajectories rather than discrete group transfer
Main difference from LA-KAIE: Interaction estimated from population data without extra FEs (similar spirit to LA-KAIE's estimator). No information exchange between heterogeneous populations, no adaptive mode controller.

Paper: Exploiting linkage information in real-valued optimization with RV-GOMEA (GECCO 2017) and follow-ups (conditional linkage models, GECCO 2020; fitness-based linkage learning, IEEE TEVC 2021)
RL/learning mechanism: Linkage model learned from population (or fitness-based linkage learning); no RL
Group-wise exchange: YES - both univariate and multivariate subsets are mixed (dimension AND group level)
Main difference from LA-KAIE: CLOSE OVERLAP on group-level vs dimension-level mixing driven by learned linkage. GOMEA iterates over all FOS elements deterministically (no landscape-conditioned choice of granularity, no two-population source selection); fitness-based linkage learning costs extra evaluations.

Paper: Adaptive Linkage Crossover, Evolutionary Computation 8(3) (MIT Press)
RL/learning mechanism: Adaptive linkage matrix evolved with the population
Main difference from LA-KAIE: Early linkage-matrix crossover; no controller, no landscape state, no heterogeneous hybrid.

Paper: Landscape-Aware Bandit Hyper-Heuristics for Online Operator Selection in UAV Inspection Routing (LA-BHH), arXiv 2605.14620
Landscape awareness: YES - static landscape descriptors + online search-state features incl. stagnation
Knowledge-aware reward: Improvement rewards (single objective component per snippet)
Main difference from LA-KAIE: CLOSE on the controller concept (landscape-aware contextual bandit choosing operators online). Different domain, no variable-interaction model, no cross-population exchange. Also shares the 'LA-' prefix - naming collision risk.

Paper: RL-HPSDE: Differential evolution with hybrid parameters and mutation strategies based on reinforcement learning, Swarm and Evolutionary Computation
Landscape awareness: YES - dynamic fitness-distance correlation and ruggedness define 4 states
Main difference from LA-KAIE: Landscape-state RL controller already exists for operator selection. No interaction model, no group exchange, no heterogeneous two-population hybrid.

Paper: Sharma, Komninos, Lopez-Ibanez, Kazakov - Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Parameter Control in Differential Evolution (DE-DDQN), GECCO 2019
RL/learning mechanism: Double deep Q-network trained offline, applied online
Landscape awareness: YES - 99 state features incl. landscape features
Main difference from LA-KAIE: Landscape-feature state for operator selection (offline-trained deep model). No interaction groups, no cross-population exchange.

Paper: Reinforcement Learning-based Self-adaptive Differential Evolution through Automated Landscape Feature Learning (arXiv 2503.18061)
Main difference from LA-KAIE: Landscape-aware RL control of DE; no interaction-group exchange or heterogeneous two-population information exchange.

Paper: An interactive evolutionary multitask optimization algorithm for variables group-level knowledge transfer (EMTO-IVG), Applied Soft Computing
RL/learning mechanism: Transfer strategy adjusted via user interaction
Main difference from LA-KAIE: Group-level transfer exists in multitask optimization (between tasks, user-in-the-loop). LA-KAIE transfers within one task between two heterogeneous optimizers with an automatic controller.

Paper: Differential grouping family (DG / DG2 / Extended DG / Enhanced DG) for cooperative co-evolution
Main difference from LA-KAIE: Interaction detection costs extra FEs and is used for decomposition, not for adaptive cross-population exchange.
